anomalies.observed: The CAN transceivers’ GND1 and GND2 pins are both connected to GND, so the two sides of each transceiver’s isolation barrier share a ground net. The bus-side supply is also labeled 5V_switched_CAN, not a separate isolated supply.
anomalies.expected: The CAN interfaces are specified as isolated. Their logic-side and bus-side grounds and supplies should remain galvanically separated, with an isolated supply for the bus side.

evidence.quote: U11: GND1, GND2; both pins connect to GND (sheet cm4-robot.kicad_sch, page 1).
U10: GND1, GND2; both pins connect to GND (sheet cm4-robot.kicad_sch, page 1).

anomalies.impact: The CAN interfaces lose galvanic isolation, allowing ground differences and faults on the bus side to couple into the logic-side ground and undermining the intended isolation protection.

parsed.summary: The schematic connects both ground pins of each CAN isolation transceiver to the same GND net, contrary to the specified isolated CAN interfaces. This defeats galvanic isolation on both buses.
